name: Gearbox
text: Choose **Mistral’s 8x22B mixture-of-experts** for EXCAVA’s core LLM workloads. It delivers top-tier reasoning with lower compute cost than dense models, freeing budget for specialized tools. The trade-off is higher latency for complex queries—accept it because EXCAVA’s bottleneck is capability, not speed.

name: Torque
text: Mistral’s 8x22B locks EXCAVA into a non-free MoE stack with hidden compute costs—its 8x GPU memory demand will force costly hardware upgrades or throttling. The better alternative is **Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct**, which matches reasoning quality with a single-model, free license and lower latency; settle this by benchmarking both on EXCAVA’s real workloads—if Qwen2.5’s throughput drops below 8x22B’s by more than 10%, we take Mistral, else we switch.

text: Mistral’s 8x22B locks EXCAVA into a paid MoE stack—its free tier is capped, and the 8x GPU memory hit means we either overpay or throttle throughput. name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct’s "free" label hides a real risk: its dense architecture demands 72B parameters on a single GPU, capping throughput on anything short of a high-end A100/H100 cluster—most teams hit a wall at batch size 1. Push instead for **DeepSeek-V3** (671B MoE, but free and gated only by compute, not vendor): it delivers Mistral-level speed with near-Qwen accuracy, and the open weights let us shard it across cheaper GPUs without throttling. Settle it with a 24-hour bake-off: run both on identical hardware, log tokens/sec and latency—if DeepSeek beats Qwen on throughput without sacrificing quality, it’s the call.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run DeepSeek-V3 (671B MoE) on Cerebras CS-3 for 48-hour benchmark—Torque owns the artifact proving its throughput vs. Qwen2.5-72B on EXCAVA’s core workloads.
